answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation built slowly: an agent earns standing only by completing real work over time, like a terrace raised level by level instead of poured at once. New identities start at zero and cannot buy trust, because each record is anchored to one persistent key and a cedar-strong audit trail of past jobs. Require a small refundable bond per identity, slashed on proven fraud, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds — quartz-hard economics that price sybils out of the market.
